text: Started outlining the novel tonight. A lighthouse keeper who receives letters from a version of herself that never left the mainland. I don't know the ending yet and that's exciting.
Ran the ridge trail for the first time this year. Legs are not ready but the view at the top never gets old.
Wrote the opening scene of the novel. The lighthouse keeper finds the first letter tucked into a delivery of oil for the lamp. Two thousand words, roughest draft imaginable, but it exists now.
Had a rough day at work. My manager keeps changing priorities mid-sprint and I'm starting to wonder if this team is sustainable long term.
Called Mom for her birthday, talked for an hour. She's finally getting the garden fence fixed after two summers of complaining about the deer.
Novel: figured out the antagonist isn't a person, it's the tide schedule itself. The letters only arrive during the lowest tides of the year. Structural constraint, love it.
Hiking with Dana on Saturday, she wants to attempt the full loop before it gets too hot. I said yes before thinking it through.
Character work on the novel today. Her name is Mireille. She hasn't left the island in eleven years and everyone in the village has a theory about why.
Back at the gym after a long gap. Everything that used to be easy is not easy anymore, humbling.
Updated my resume for the first time in three years. It's humbling how much I've forgotten I even did.
Draft of chapter three of the novel. The other-self letters start contradicting each other and Mireille has to decide which life she trusts more.
Did the full loop. Nine miles, way harder than I remembered, my knees are filing a complaint.
Novel is stalling a bit — chapter four keeps wanting to be a flashback and I don't think it should be. Pushed through 800 words anyway.
Dad sent a long email about a project he's doing in the garage, restoring an old radio. He's happiest when he has something to take apart.
Talked to a recruiter about a role at a smaller company. More ownership, less process, but also less stability. Don't know yet.
Big novel breakthrough at 1am: the letters aren't from another timeline, they're from her future self, sent backward through the lighthouse lamp somehow. Rewriting chapter one tomorrow.
Short trail run before work today. Saw a family of deer right at the switchback. Good way to start a Monday.
Gym three times this week, which is a record for the year so far.
Rewrote the novel's opening with the new future-self concept. So much better. Sent the first three chapters to my writing group for feedback.
Second interview went fine I think? Hard to read the room over video calls. Trying not to obsess over it.
Writing group liked the novel pages a lot, said Mireille needs a stronger want in chapter two. Taking notes, feeling motivated.
Rain cancelled the weekend hike. Did a treadmill run instead which is objectively worse in every way but at least kept the streak alive.
Sunday call with the family, my sister announced she's moving cities for a new job. Everyone's excited and a little sad at the same time.
Only wrote 300 words on the novel today, work was exhausting. Chapter five is proving hard because it's the first time Mireille lies to someone.
Didn't get the job. Disappointed but honestly relieved too — the pay bump wasn't enough to offset how chaotic that team sounded in the loop.
Haven't touched the novel in a week. Feeling guilty about it but also just tired. Maybe outline chapter six this weekend instead of drafting.
New trail today, the one past the reservoir. Quieter than the ridge, way fewer people, might be my new favorite.
Skipped the gym for two weeks straight, work got in the way. Going back tomorrow, no more excuses.
Opened the novel document, stared at it, closed it again. I think I need a break from Mireille for a bit, not abandoning it, just resting.
Work has been calmer this month. Maybe I don't need to leave, maybe I just needed a slower sprint.
Mom's garden fence is finally done. She sent seventeen photos of it from every angle, which is extremely her.
Running has been rough this month, motivation is low. Made myself do a short easy loop just to not lose the habit entirely.
Weird 2am thought: if a lighthouse sends light out in a rotating beam, is the darkness between beams also a kind of signal? Not sure why this felt profound at the time.
Good lift today, hit a new number on the deadlift that I've been chasing for months.
Asked for a stretch project on the platform team. Scary to raise my hand but I want more technical depth, not just glue work.
Signed up for a half marathon in October. Terrifying commitment device but I think I need one.
Helped Dad troubleshoot his radio project over video call, mostly by pointing at the screen and going 'is that wire supposed to be there.'
Bought a used acoustic guitar on a whim. No idea if I'll stick with it but the store guy was very patient with my terrible strumming.
Got the stretch project. Nervous-excited. First design doc due next week.
Learned my first three chords today. G, C, and D. My fingertips currently hate me.
First real training run for the half marathon. Pace felt slow but the plan says that's the point right now.
Gym has started feeling like a habit instead of a chore, which took way longer than I expected.
Practiced for twenty minutes, fingers hurt less. Can almost switch between G and C without stopping the strum.
Idea I can't stop thinking about: a small business teaching people to fix their own bikes, run out of the garage on weekends. Probably nothing. Writing it down anyway.
Long overdue call with my sister in her new city. She sounds lighter than she has in years. Good decision, clearly.
Learned a fourth chord, Em, and can now technically play about six songs badly. Very proud of this.
Presented my design doc today. Survived thirty minutes of questions from the staff engineers and only had to say 'let me get back to you' twice.
Tried to play along with a song for the first time. It was a disaster and also the most fun I've had all week.
Long run day, 8 miles, and for the first time in weeks I actually enjoyed it instead of just gritting through it.
Callus check: my fingertips are finally toughening up. Practice doesn't hurt anymore, just feels hard in a normal way.
Family group chat blew up over nothing, as usual, resolved itself within an hour, also as usual.
Learned a barre chord. It sounded like a dying cat for the first ten tries and then suddenly, briefly, like an actual chord.
Design doc got approved with minor changes. First real system I get to own end to end. Trying to actually feel proud instead of immediately worrying about launch.
Tried a new gym class with Dana before our run. Different muscles complaining today, in a good way.
Trail run with Dana again, first time in months. She's training for the same half marathon, didn't even plan that, just happened.
Played through a full song front to back without stopping for the first time. Recorded it as proof to future me who won't believe it.
Read something about octopuses possibly dreaming in color-changing patterns across their skin and now I can't think about anything else.
Planning a trip home for the holidays already, feels early but flights get expensive if I wait.
Launch prep for the platform project starting. Equal parts thrilled and terrified, which I think is just what caring about your work feels like.
Guitar practice at night has become my favorite part of the day, somehow. Didn't expect that when I bought it.
